sections.h2: What is the simplest way to sell a house in Columbia, TN?
sections.html:
The simplest way is a direct cash purchase, where the buyer needs no mortgage approval and takes the house in its current condition. If the house is in good shape and you have a few months, an agent listing can reach more buyers, and an owner sale cuts out the commission.

Columbia is the seat of Maury County and part of the Nashville metropolitan area, on the south bank of the Duck River. The Census Bureau counted 41,690 residents in April 2020 and estimates 50,072 for July 1, 2025, a rise of 20.3% from its 2020 estimates base.

  • Cash buyer: fewest steps, no repairs, and a price that reflects the house as it stands.
  • Listing: more exposure, with inspections, showings and a buyer's financing to manage.
  • Owner sale: no commission, but you handle pricing, disclosure and the contract.

Before you choose, get a payoff figure from your mortgage servicer and a tax balance from the Maury County Trustee.

sections.h2: How does Columbia compare with nearby cities on housing costs?
sections.html:
Columbia's Census numbers sit in the middle range. The typical owned home is valued at $308,700 for 2020 to 2024, 63.3% of housing units are owner-occupied, and median gross rent is $1,197 a month. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,548, and those without one report $469.

sections.h2: What is Columbia known for, and how does that affect a sale?
sections.html:
Columbia calls itself the mule capital of the world and holds Mule Day every April. The city and Maury County are also described as the Antebellum Homes Capital of Tennessee, and Columbia has one of the last two surviving residences of President James K. Polk. Heritage tourism is a real part of the local economy.

Columbia was laid out in 1808 and incorporated in 1817, and Union troops burned Jackson College and most of the city during the Civil War. If your house is old, ask the city planning office whether any historic-district rules apply to your address before you tell a buyer what they may change on the exterior.

Columbia State Community College, Tennessee's first two-year college, was established in 1966 and serves nine counties in southern Middle Tennessee. Maury County Public Schools operates the public schools, and private options include Columbia Academy, Zion Christian Academy and Agathos Classical School.

sections.h2: What land and climate details matter for a Columbia house?
sections.html:
Columbia grew along the Duck River at the southern edge of the Nashville Basin, at an elevation of about 637 feet, with the Highland Rim rising to the south and west. The city covers roughly 29.6 square miles. The Duck River is the longest river entirely inside Tennessee, so buyers near it may ask about flood zones and insurance.

The climate is humid subtropical, with hot, humid summers and mild to cool winters. The 1991 to 2020 normals at a station near Columbia show about 56.8 inches of precipitation in a year, with December the wettest month at 5.64 inches. The average daily high reaches 88.8 degrees Fahrenheit in July and the average low drops to 26.9 degrees in January.

  • Check the roof, gutters and drainage after the wet months.
  • Ask your insurer whether the lot sits in a mapped flood area.
  • Keep records of any HVAC replacement, since summer heat is long.

sections.h2: When are Maury County property taxes due in Columbia?
sections.html:
The Maury County Trustee collects real and personal property tax, with notices mailed in October to the owner of record as of January 1. The payment window runs from the first Monday of October through the last day of February without penalty. On March 1, county taxes become delinquent and a 1.5% penalty and interest begins, rising each month, and delinquent accounts are turned over to Chancery Court on April 1.

The office accepts partial payments, though interest applies to any unpaid balance on March 1. Online payments carry a 2.5% vendor fee, which the county says does not go to its office. The trustee sits at One Public Square, Columbia, phone 931-375-2201, open weekdays 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Postmarks are honored except once delinquent taxes go to Chancery Court.

Tennessee law does not require the mailing of tax notices, so a missing bill is not a reason to skip payment. The Maury County Trustee page lists these terms.

sections.h2: Does a Columbia reappraisal change what I owe?
sections.html:
It can. The Maury County Assessor, at 6 Public Square (931-375-4001), sets appraised values based on market value as of January 1 of the last reappraisal year, plus the equalized value of any improvements added since. Maury County reappraises every four years, and 2026 is the current reappraisal year.

To estimate a bill, multiply the appraised value by the assessment ratio for the property's class, then multiply by the tax rate, which the Maury County Commission sets. An owner who thinks the value is unfair can appeal to the local board of equalization, and then to the State Board of Equalization. Details are on the Maury County Assessor page.

If you are selling in a reappraisal year, mention the new value to your closing company, since the buyer will want to know what the next bill might look like.

sections.h2: How is a Columbia deed recorded?
sections.html:
The Maury County Register of Deeds, a constitutional office regulated by state statute, records your deed and keeps the permanent record. The county's quick links include a fee calculator for recording costs. State recordation tax, which combines a realty transfer tax and a mortgage tax, is collected by the register for the Department of Revenue, as described on the state recordation tax page.

Ask the register or your closing company for the exact recording cost on your deed. If the property passed to you from a relative, bring the probate paperwork so the title company can confirm who may sign.

faqs.q: How soon can a cash sale close on a Columbia house?
faqs.a: As soon as title work is clear and every owner can sign. With no lender involved, the timeline depends on the title search, any probate and lien payoffs, so ask your closing company for a date.

faqs.q: When does Maury County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: On March 1, after the payment window that ends the last day of February. A 1.5% penalty and interest begins that day and rises monthly, and unpaid accounts go to Chancery Court on April 1.

faqs.q: How often does Maury County reappraise property?
faqs.a: Every four years, and 2026 is the current reappraisal year. Owners who disagree can appeal to the local board of equalization and then the State Board of Equalization.

faqs.q: Can I make partial property tax payments in Maury County?
faqs.a: Yes. The trustee accepts partial payments, but interest applies to any unpaid balance on March 1.

faqs.q: Which office records my Columbia deed?
faqs.a: The Maury County Register of Deeds. It records the document and keeps the permanent record, and it collects the state recordation tax on the instrument.
